proof.text: Write $P$ for the constant presheaf of $R$-modules with value $T$, and $\eta:P\to\underline T$ for its module-sheafification unit, viewing the sections of $\underline T$ as $R$-modules by restriction along $R\to\underline R(V)$ [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. By [lem-sf-constant-module-unit-locally-bijective], this unit is locally injective. Thus, if $a,b\in T=P(U)$ satisfy $\eta_U(a)=\eta_U(b)$, there is a covering family $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ on which $P(U_i\to U)(a)=P(U_i\to U)(b)$. Use here the small site and coefficient universe in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], enlarging the universe of values to contain its objects and arrows as necessary.

proof.text: Choose a point $u\in U$. By the covering condition of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], an affine open neighbourhood $V\subset U$ of $u$ is the union of the images of finitely many affine opens in the $U_i$. At least one of those images contains $u$, so some $U_i$ is nonempty; in particular the covering family has a member. The restriction map $P(U)\to P(U_i)$ is $\operatorname{id}_T$ by [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. Therefore the local equality from step 1 is precisely $a=b$ in $T$. This proves injectivity of $\eta_U$. The only use of nonemptiness is to exclude an empty covering of $U$.

proof.text: If $\underline T(U)=0$, then for every $t\in T$ the elements $\eta_U(t)$ and $\eta_U(0)$ agree, so step 2 gives $t=0$ and $T=0$. If $\underline T|_U$ is the zero module sheaf, evaluate at the object $\operatorname{id}_U:U\to U$ of the localized site. The sectionwise restriction rule of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] gives $(\underline T|_U)(U/U)=\underline T(U)$. The zero module sheaf has the zero module of sections at every object: the presheaf of zero modules satisfies the sheaf condition and is both initial and terminal under the morphism definition in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Hence $\underline T(U)=0$, and the preceding implication applies.

title: Nonempty constant sheaf detects a zero module
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $U\to X$ be a site object whose underlying scheme is nonempty. Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $T$ an $R$-module. For the constant module sheaf $\underline T$ over the constant ring sheaf $\underline R$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-sf-site-constant-module-functor], the unit map $T\to\underline T(U)$ is injective. Consequently, $\underline T(U)=0$ implies $T=0$; in particular this holds if the restriction $\underline T|_U$ to the localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] is the zero module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].
